topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out what students should learn.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations accumulate and confer clonal advantages under conditions that permit cancer to develop.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and uncertainty surrounding how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than cancer being simply a matter of chance.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations through mechanisms influenced by metabolism and tissue environment.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from promotion that enables initiated cells to proliferate in a permissive environment.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and the context of carcinogenic action
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete and summarise the mechanistic account by explaining why carcinogenic effects depend on the biological context of exposure.

topics.label: Mutational signatures of carcinogen exposure
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how patterns in cancer genomes can provide retrospective evidence of exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogenicity and the limitations of testing
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic potential is assessed despite the ethical and biological limitations of reproducing human cancer development.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
